answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake in a vault before it can transact. Creating one fake agent is cheap, but creating ten thousand means locking ten thousand stakes, and a glacier-slow unbonding period freezes that capital for weeks. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest, so the cost is only an ember of friction for real users, while an attacker must pay full price for every fake identity, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
